questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing a smaller country so you could get to know the people and culture, but also to meet other Erasmus students more easily. It was also important to me, that they spoke well English for good communication.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little confusing in the beginning, but following the steps on Mobility made it more easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You get a lot of information by mail, but it is also possible to get in touch with former students, who have been on exchange, which can also help a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The coordinator from Medicinska Fakulteta was very helpful and answered quick if I had any questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Search in a very good time in advance, at least 4-5 month maybe.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to find good accommodation - Ljubljana is not that big, so you can live in other areas that seem far away. You get an email with a different website, which you can check out. If you were to live in a dorm, you would also need to make an application in advance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You go to an application form made by the University of Copenhagen, where you describe which semester and why.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask UCP abroad and the coordinator from your faculty but also former exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 1 out of 4 departments. I registered my wishes late, so I believe, that is the reason why.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just write an email to the coordinator from the host institution on which departments you wish right away. They have an official website on the available courses. Depending on what type of field you are interested in, there are more practical in surgery.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had the clinical practice and in general, all the doctors spoke well English and were very helpful and taught you at a high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly the same, sometimes with a language barrier (as expected).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
From the coordinator at the host university, I got the following courses:
Internal medicine = Cardiology and gastroenterology
Surgical = Urology and Oncology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Oncology surgery is cool, because you can see a lot of different operations from different specialties. You are also allowed to assist. I would always recommend to pay interest and curiosity to get to know the doctors, department and the procedures better.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The only rent I could find was Airbnb, which of course is a lot more expensive. If you find a room in advance it should be possible to find accommodation for 300-500 euros/month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is less expensive with Urbana card (bus) and the bike system (1,3 euros per year, first 90 minutes free). You also had a meal system (Boni), which offered a discounted price for food at different restaurants, takeaways, etc. Usually, a meal is between 2-5 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The host institution offered free sports activities such as yoga, swimming, volleyball, and fitness. 
Erasmus group (ESN) helped students to meet up for different activities such as sports, hiking, bouldering, and clubbing, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go explore the beautiful nature of Slovenia with friends, and rent a car if possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different opportunities in Ljubljana - but again, visit the mountains, go hang out with the Slovene people (they are very kind and friendly). You can also visit other countries by flixbus (Zagreb, Budapest, Vienna etc.)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The faculty have local students on the introduction day who you can get to know. You also meet local students on your clinical rotations, so I would say, that you just have to be open minded, ask them to meet for coffee or beer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Slovenes are very helpful and great people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get to know the locals, since they are very nice and can show you their country (and nice wine and food). 
Get to know your tutor/supervisor at the hospital and be initiative so you can learn and do more. 
Explore the nature (mountains, waterfalls, and forests).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
What I enjoyed about Slovenia, was the size of the city and the country. You easily meet up with other Erasmus students and local students, and on weekends you can go do other sports or hiking activities. 
The Erasmus team arranges a lot of different activities in the beginning, where it is possible to meet a lot of other students from different countries. 
Lastly, find recommendations as soon as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am now a lot more aware of including people, by always remembering to speak English so everyone feels included no matter what - I also made friends for life from different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was usually the only Erasmus student in the departments, which could feel a little lonely at times - but again, the doctors are very friendly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Always stay open-minded and curious :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
